stages.title: Be honest — how many have you opened?
stages.desc: Copilot reads every one of these files before it suggests a single line. Let’s open them, one by one.

stages.title: File 1: it never forgets the rules
stages.desc: copilot-instructions.md rides along on every request — the closest thing Copilot has to memory.

stages.title: File 2: rules that know the file type
stages.desc: instructions/*.instructions.md scopes different rules to different paths with one glob.

stages.title: File 3: skills that load themselves
stages.desc: SKILL.md bundles instructions, scripts and resources — Copilot pulls it in the moment your ask matches, no slash command required.

stages.title: File 4: chat gets a persona
stages.desc: A custom agent packages its own tools, model and instructions into one dropdown option.

stages.title: File 5: the agent's launchpad
stages.desc: copilot-setup-steps.yml preinstalls everything before the autonomous coding agent starts work.

stages.title: File 6: flip the switches
stages.desc: settings.json turns Copilot features on or off, per workspace, without touching code.

stages.title: File 7: it can touch real systems
stages.desc: mcp.json connects Copilot to your database, Jira or an internal API as callable tools.

stages.title: That's the whole rulebook
stages.desc: Seven files, all versioned in your repo — nothing hidden inside the model.

end.title: Now you know all seven
end.sub: Versioned, reviewable, yours to edit — that's Copilot's real rulebook.

post.caption: Quick test: how many of these 7 files have you actually opened? GitHub Copilot reads every one of them before it suggests a single line — memory, per-path rules, self-loading skills, custom agents, coding-agent setup, workspace switches, and MCP tools. Here's exactly what each one does.

learn: copilot-instructions.md is auto-attached to every chat request — repo-wide, no reference needed
instructions/*.instructions.md scopes rules per path, skills/SKILL.md loads itself when your ask matches, and agents/*.agent.md (formerly chat modes) packages personas per task
mcp.json and copilot-setup-steps.yml extend Copilot into real tools and give the autonomous coding agent its own preinstalled sandbox

faq.q: What files does GitHub Copilot actually read from a repository?
faq.a: Up to seven, when a repo uses all of them: .github/copilot-instructions.md for repo-wide rules, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md for path-scoped rules via an applyTo glob, .github/skills/*/SKILL.md for self-loading agent skills, .github/agents/*.agent.md for custom agents, .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml to provision the coding agent's sandbox, .vscode/settings.json for workspace feature switches, and .vscode/mcp.json to register MCP servers.

faq.q: Are GitHub Copilot chat modes the same thing as custom agents?
faq.a: Yes — VS Code renamed chat modes to custom agents in 2026. Existing *.chatmode.md files still work, but the current format is *.agent.md in .github/agents, and the picker now reads "Configure Custom Agents" instead of "Configure Chat Modes."

faq.q: Do GitHub Copilot prompt files still work?
faq.a: They still run under the Local agent, but VS Code has deprecated *.prompt.md for Agent Host sessions in favor of Agent Skills. A SKILL.md folder bundles instructions, scripts and resources, and Copilot loads it automatically once your request matches its description — you can also still call it manually by typing /.
